name: effects
character: The effect library of scripts/fx_engine: every effect's parameters, their ranges and their defaults. A chain in an instrument preset (`fx`) names effects from here.
provenance: starting value: every default and range below is a working figure chosen so the effect is audible and safe on a stem, not a measurement. Physical relations (the Doppler delay is path length over the speed of sound, a wow depth in cents follows from the delay swing) are derived in the code from the parameters; the numbers are not. Replace one with a measured or cited value in a project's own `fx` preset and say so there. Automation and recipes: starting values drawn from practitioner guidance (ramping an LFO's rate and depth together on a riser, automating distortion or filter for movement, saving the biggest impacts for the climax; Ableton 'Learn How to Make High-Impact Sounds for Movies and Trailers', Violet Recording 'Sound Design for Trailers'); not measurements.

start_s.text: where the effect begins, in stem time

end_s.text: where it ends; none means the end of the stem

edge_ms.text: raised-cosine crossfade at both ends of the range

seed.text: random seed of this effect; none derives one from the stem

automate.text: parameters that move over the effect range: {"rate_hz": {"from": 0.5, "to": 12.0, "curve": "exp"}} or keyframes {"depth": [[0, 0.1], [0.6, 0.4], [1, 0.9]]} (time as a fraction of the range); only on an effect marked "automatable"

steps.text: how many slices an automated range is cut into; each slice runs the effect with that slice's values and the slices cross-fade

tape_stop.character: The tape slows to a halt: pitch and level fall to nothing over dur_s, then silence.

dur_s.text: time from full speed to stopped

curve.text: speed = (1 - t)^curve: above 1 the slow-down is back-loaded

level_pow.text: level follows speed^level_pow so the held sample does not leave a DC step

pitch_glide.character: A pitch dive or riser: playback speed glides by `semitones` over the range, then the dry signal returns.

semitones.text: pitch change reached at end_s (negative dives)

doppler.character: A pass-by: the source travels past the listener at speed_m_s, with the delay, pitch change and level the path length gives.

speed_m_s.text: speed of the source along its straight path

pass_s.text: time of closest approach; none is the middle of the range

c_m_s.text: speed of sound; none reads the active medium (phys_core.medium)

edge_ms.text: fade in from and out to the dry stem: the pass starts far away and quiet, so the edge is long

tape_wobble.character: Wow and flutter: slow and fast pitch drift of an old transport, set in cents.

wow_cents.text: peak pitch deviation of the slow drift

flutter_cents.text: peak pitch deviation of the fast drift

stutter.character: Beat repeat: the first slice of the range repeats until the range ends, each repeat a little quieter.

freeze.character: Spectral freeze: the sound at start_s is held for hold_s as a smooth, phase-randomised wash.

hold_s.text: how long the frozen sound is held

fft.text: analysis size: a larger one is smoother and slower to bloom

edge_ms.text: crossfade of the frozen wash with the dry stem

grain_cloud.character: A cloud of short grains read from the stem around their own position, scattered in pitch and place.

pitch_spread_cents.text: random pitch scatter of a grain

pos_spread_s.text: how far from its own time a grain may read

pan_spread.text: random placement of a grain between the channels

level_db.text: cloud level against the stem's own level in the range

filter_sweep.character: A filter whose cutoff glides between two frequencies over the range: the riser sweep and the downlifter.

curve.text: how the cutoff moves: exp is even in octaves

after.text: after end_s: the dry stem, or the filter held at f_end_hz

ring_mod.character: Ring modulation: the stem multiplied by a sine, for bell-like, metallic or robotic colour.

tremolo.character: Amplitude tremolo, and an auto-pan when pan_depth is above zero.

pan_depth.text: how far the sound swings between the channels (opposite phase left to right)

gate_pulse.character: A rhythmic gate: the stem chopped by a pulse of a given rate and duty.

duty.text: share of each pulse that is open

reverse_swell.character: A reverse reverb: a swell that builds into every note, made by reverberating the reversed stem.

decay_s.text: length of the swell (time to -60 dB)

wet_db.text: swell level against the stem's own level

shimmer.character: A shimmering reverb: the tail is pitched up and fed back, so each repeat sits an octave above the last.

shift_semitones.text: pitch step of each feedback pass

feedback.text: level of the pitched tail fed back

wet_db.text: shimmer level against the stem's own level

transient.character: Transient shaper: sharpen or soften the front of a note, and lift or tuck its body.

attack_db.text: gain on the front of a note

sustain_db.text: gain on the body after the front

pedalboard.character: Any built-in Pedalboard plugin in the chain: Chorus, Phaser, Delay, Reverb, Distortion, Bitcrush, LadderFilter, PitchShift and the rest of the allow-list.

params.text: constructor arguments of the plugin, by name

external.character: A real VST3 or Audio Unit plugin on disk, loaded through Pedalboard, with its parameters set by name. The one way to add a compiled third-party effect.

path.text: file of the plugin; it must exist

air.character: Air exciter: adds harmonics above a corner from the band that exists, for samples that hold nothing above 8 kHz. It creates content; it is not an EQ, and it is measured by realism.air.

corner_hz.text: the band at and above this frequency feeds the exciter

drive.text: saturation drive of the excited band

amount_db.text: level of the added harmonics under the stem
